hints.title: Longest Common Subsequence Isomorphism
hints.text: Drawing non-crossing lines between identical values in nums1 and nums2 requires both chosen index sequences to be strictly increasing, which is mathematically identical to finding their longest common subsequence.

hints.title: DP Transition Rules
hints.text: If nums1[i - 1] == nums2[j - 1], the line can be formed: dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1. Otherwise, skip one element: dp[i][j] = max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]).

hints.title: Space Optimization
hints.text: Because each cell in the DP table depends only on the previous row, compress the 2D grid into a 1D array of length n + 1.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursively checking all subsets of matches has exponential complexity O(2^(M+N)).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Standard dynamic programming tabulation runs in O(M * N) time and can be compressed to O(N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that non-crossing lines between arrays is equivalent to LCS.
